content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The mobile Linux operating system postmarketOS has officially changed its name to Nura, according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/postmarketos-is-now-nura-after-major-project-rebrand/), ending a naming process that lasted roughly a year and a half. Linuxiac reports that the project announced the new name during its conference, and that references to postmarketOS will remain in documentation, packages, websites, and other places while the transition completes.

editor_notes.source_verification: Read sources/2026-09/postmarketos-rebrands-as-nura-after-an-18-month-naming-process-citing-trademark-and-pronunciation-problems/source-0.html.gz (Linuxiac, HTTP 200, byline dated September 27, 2026). It confirms verbatim: name change; 'a naming process that lasted roughly a year and a half'; announced 'today during its conference'; references remaining in documentation, packages, websites; Nura short for 'Nuraghe' (ancient stone structures in Sardinia); old name long and hard to pronounce/remember in some languages; unusual capitalization (PostmarketOS, PostMarketOS); descriptive old name no longer reflects scope, PinePhones sold with postmarketOS preinstalled; descriptive name cannot be trademarked and a trademark application for Nura was filed; more than 300 community names, multiple rounds, four finalists checked for problematic meanings in other languages, internal team vote where Nura received the highest result; logo kept with increased arrow spacing and mathematical reconstruction; nura.eco, nura.org already owned and not purchasable at a reasonable price; nothing changes for end users. The Linuxiac snapshot does NOT contain the three claims cited to AlternativeTo (March 2025 teaser with trademark/consensus delays; .eco aligning with environmental mission; goal of reaching beyond the hacker community). The AlternativeTo snapshot failed (manifest: file null, HTTP 403 Forbidden), so as a last resort I used WebFetch on the live URL (snapshot failed; live URL used instead). WebFetch returned: 'The rebranding was first teased in March 2025, though delays due to trademark considerations and the need to build consensus within the community pushed the official reveal to the present day.'; 'the .eco extension aligns with the project's environmental mission'; and 'aiming to expand recognition beyond the traditional hacker community that has supported the project since its inception.' These match the article's attributions. Caveat: WebFetch is LLM-mediated and not archived in provenance; the AlternativeTo-cited claims are subordinate (timeline, domain rationale, stated goal), are attributed to AlternativeTo, and the .eco/domain context is consistent with Linuxiac's nura.org/.eco account. No claim in the headline, summary or lead rests on AlternativeTo. Nothing rests on the unlisted nura.eco announcement (Linuxiac links it but the article does not cite it). Date Sept 27, 2026, 18-month process, trademark and pronunciation reasons, and the team-vote details all verified against Linuxiac. suspicious_patterns: none on the Linuxiac source (null); the 403 source has no snapshot to scan.
